question: What is the final phase of the classic nursing management process?
explanation: Controlling comes last in the management cycle to check if plans were successfully carried out. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why are benchmarks necessary for the controlling function in a hospital?

options.A: They measure performance against expected goals
options.B: They replace the need for direct staff supervision
options.C: They dictate the hospital annual financial budget
options.D: They automatically hire new clinical nursing staff

explanation: Benchmarks give managers a clear standard to compare actual nursing work against. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: What do performance standards primarily describe in a healthcare setting?

options.A: The exact salary scale for nursing officers
options.B: The daily menu for hospitalized patients
options.C: The minimum acceptable level of care
options.D: The architectural design of the ward

explanation: Performance standards outline the baseline quality of care every nurse must deliver. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: How do clinical performance standards protect the practicing nurse?

options.A: By preventing patients from filing formal complaints
options.B: By removing the need for professional licensing exams
options.C: By guaranteeing immunity from all hospital errors
options.D: By clearly outlining the expected scope of duty

explanation: Knowing the exact standard of practice helps nurses prove they acted correctly within their legal boundaries. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: A nurse-to-patient ratio of 1:5 is an example of which type of standard?
explanation: Quantitative standards deal with countable numbers, ratios, and measurable frequencies. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: A head nurse assessing how gently staff speak to anxious surgical patients is evaluating what type of standard?
explanation: Qualitative standards focus on the character, demeanor, and human experience of care delivery. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is a key requirement of an effective nursing standard regarding resources?

options.A: It requires unlimited funding from the federal government
options.B: It must be achievable with available resources
options.C: It should ignore local resource limitations entirely
options.D: It must rely solely on imported medical equipment

explanation: Standards fail if they demand resources that the local facility or environment does not possess. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why must nursing standards be specific and clear?

options.A: To eliminate the need for ongoing professional training
options.B: To prevent confusion and ensure consistent clinical practice
options.C: To ensure only senior doctors can interpret the rules
options.D: To make nursing manuals as long and detailed as possible

explanation: Clear wording ensures all nurses interpret and execute the procedure in the exact same safe manner. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is the very first step in establishing a new clinical nursing standard?

options.D: Punishing staff who fail old routines

explanation: Standards must be rooted in solid clinical evidence before any drafting or testing begins. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: Why is pilot testing a new standard in one ward recommended before hospital-wide introduction?

options.A: To identify practical problems before full implementation
options.B: To ensure only junior nurses have to follow the rules
options.C: To hide the new changes from senior hospital management
options.D: To delay the administrative workload for as long as possible

explanation: Testing a standard on a small scale allows managers to fix flaws before launching it everywhere. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: Which body is primarily responsible for setting the legal scope of nursing practice in Nigeria?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body empowered to regulate nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: Why must hospital-level nursing standards align with national regulatory guidelines?

options.A: To reduce the monthly salary budget of the hospital
options.B: To eliminate the need for internal ward supervision
options.C: To prevent foreign nurses from working in local wards
options.D: To maintain legal accreditation and protect public safety

explanation: Compliance with national bodies ensures hospitals operate legally and deliver safe patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to implementing nursing standards in Nigeria?

options.A: Severe staff burnout from high patient ratios
options.B: Resistance to change among experienced personnel
options.C: Excessive availability of advanced medical equipment
options.D: Inconsistent power and water supply in wards

explanation: Resource scarcity is a major challenge, so excessive equipment availability is contrary to reality. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: How does chronic staff shortage directly affect the enforcement of nursing standards?

options.A: It gives nurses more time to mentor junior colleagues
options.B: It forces exhausted nurses to take shortcuts in care
options.C: It automatically increases the quality of bedside documentation
options.D: It completely eliminates workplace conflict on the ward

explanation: When overworked, nurses often prioritize immediate survival tasks over meticulous adherence to every standard. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting routine nursing audits on a hospital ward?

options.A: To determine which nurses deserve immediate demotion
options.B: To check if clinical standards are being met in practice
options.C: To replace the need for patient admission records
options.D: To calculate the annual profit margins of the clinic

explanation: Audits evaluate actual nursing actions against established benchmarks to ensure quality. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h8)

question: When a clinical audit reveals a recurring medication error, what should be the manager's initial approach?

options.A: Immediately terminate the employment of all night nurses
options.B: Hide the report from the hospital quality committee
options.C: Conduct a root-cause analysis to find system flaws
options.D: Ignore the finding if no patient died from the error

explanation: Effective managers look for systemic issues rather than jumping straight to punitive measures. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h8)
